analysis.title: "The Pendulum Has Swung Too Far": Goldman Sees AI Capitulation As Hedge Fund Gains Evaporate
key_insights: Goldman Prime book shows hedge funds net sold global AI stocks (GSXGGLAI) for a sixth straight session, with the cumulative 6-day net flow Z-score through -3. Wilson says the cut is as extreme as anything since the launch of ChatGPT.

Wilson says momentum in price, positioning and sentiment has been abruptly negative since the end of Q2. He argues the pendulum has swung too far from indiscriminate AI enthusiasm in late Q2 to excessive pessimism now.

Hedge fund gains have reversed since June: Asia fundamental L/S is -7% MTD and +16% YTD (from +40% in June), TMT L/S is -5% MTD and +12% YTD (from +24%), global fundamental L/S is -2% MTD and +10% YTD (from +17%), and Europe L/S is flat MTD and +8% YTD.

The AI winners vs AI-at-risk pair trade had been clean for 3.5 years. It broke at the end of June after gaining more than 90% for the year and has roughly halved since. Both legs are retesting September lows after a failed rally.

CoreWeave is testing its July lows and Wilson calls it central to many of the bearish themes. The stock fell 15% on Oct 14 while its five-year CDS hit a record. Wilson says to watch whether it breaks lower next week.

Wilson names two catalysts for the week's selloff. One was CoreWeave co-founder McBee's FT comments that life insurers offer unlimited capital for AI. The other was a more urgent debate on frontier-lab business models and closed vs open model economics, including OpenAI's CFO warning companies off cheap Chinese models on Oct 14.
Wilson expects the frontier-lab debate to become far more tightly defined and transparent in coming weeks. This will shape market views on capex, credit quality and who captures economic value in AI.
Goldman credit strategists view AI-related bonds from neoclouds or frontier-lab-exposed issuers as at the epicentre of the funding cost debate.

Wilson agrees second derivatives for capex and earnings growth likely slow from here and says prices already reflect it. He says there is no evidence of slowing compute demand or compute pricing despite deep investigation.
OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar said at Goldman's conference that compute bought a year ago could be sold today for 3 to 5x, and that OpenAI is still short compute.

Wilson's key call, repeated from last week, is that leadership flips from AI spend beneficiaries to the biggest AI investors who are now revealing ROI. He expects the biggest spenders to show in Q3 earnings that they can mostly self-fund capex and are relatively immune from the value-capture debate. US mega-cap tech has broken out against the broad AI winners basket.

The 5-day sector leaderboard shows the damage concentrated in the AI supply chain: Health Care Tech +9.9% and Broadcasting +9.1% led, while Semiconductor Equipment -16.0%, Communications Equipment -13.0% and Electronic Components -12.6% lagged.

Wilson sees bonds as showing exhaustion. Yields could not rise further after CPI/PPI and broke lower on Thursday, driven by weaker-growth or financing-accident fears. The 10Y has broken below its steep uptrend line.

Goldman upgraded bonds to Overweight for the next 12 months on Monday. Wilson warns the focus on rates will persist because energy price pressures have not broken lower, with Dec WTI futures pushing toward $100 on Friday.
Wilson was surprised by how modest Goldman's USD IG and HY issuance estimates are, at roughly $2.3-2.4 trillion IG and $340-375 billion HY for this year and next, given the focus on AI financing.

Goldman's Ben Snider estimates that including expiring lockups, net US public equity supply will rise next year by the most since 2000. Wilson notes gross issuance would still be under 1% of market cap, a level routinely exceeded from the 1990s to 2022 without hurting index performance.

The author (ZeroHedge) is not ready to agree with Wilson. Funding costs do not mean-revert with positioning, and the open question is who pays for compute. Until the junk-rated end of the AI capital stack stops falling, a bounce in AI winners is a positioning trade. CoreWeave's July lows are the level to watch, and Meta reports on Oct 21.

tension_points.bull_case: Wilson says positioning is washed out, sentiment is grim, bonds look exhausted and there is no evidence of slowing compute demand or pricing. He expects leadership to flip to the biggest AI spenders as Q3 earnings show ROI.
tension_points.bear_case: The author says funding costs do not mean-revert with positioning, and the junk-rated end of the AI capital stack, such as CoreWeave's bondholders, keeps falling. Until that stops, a bounce in AI winners is a positioning trade, not a verdict.
tension_points.what_invalidates: CoreWeave breaking below its July lows next week amid broader tech weakness.
